manual.text: We used to build the world's railways because we just got on with it. The talent is still here in our towns, we’ve just let the clipboard brigade convince us we've lost our touch.

evening.text: Walked past the old steelworks tonight. We used to build the world, now we need a risk assessment to open a window. The genius is still here, we just need to trust our own backbone again.
We didn't become a brilliant country by filling in risk assessments. The ingenuity is still here, waiting in sheds and workshops. Our best days aren't in history books, they're next.

morning.text: Kettle's on. Sick of being told our best days are behind us by people who couldn't wire a plug. We've got the brains and the heritage, we just need to stop apologising and get on with it.

evening.text: We spent centuries inventing the future in drafty sheds. The talent is still here, we've just got more paperwork. Shift the red tape and we'll surprise them all again.

morning.text: We used to build railways across continents, now we get stage fright over a simple bypass. The talent and grit are still in our workshops. We just need to take the handbrake off.

evening.text: We used to build railways that changed the world on a handshake. The ingenuity is still in our towns, we just need to start trusting our own hands again instead of the clipboard brigade.
We didn't build the world's railways by being timid. The talent and grit are still here, we just need to put the clipboards down, trust our own strength, and get on with it.

morning.text: Sick of being told we’re a spent force by people who couldn't wire a plug. We didn't invent the modern world just to spend the next century apologizing for it. Kettle's on, let's get to work.

evening.text: We’ve spent too long being told we're a spent force. We aren't a museum piece just yet, we’ve just let the pessimists write the manual.

morning.text: We used to build railways with steam and grit. Now we need a three-year public consultation to fill a pothole. Time to trust ourselves and just get on with the job.

evening.text: Locking your front door isn't about hating the people outside, it's about looking after the ones inside. Used to be called common sense, not a radical opinion.
Spent all afternoon filling in compliance forms. We used to build steam engines with fewer rules than it takes to hire an apprentice today. We just need to trust folk to get on with it.

morning.text: Kettle's boiled. We didn't invent the modern world by waiting for a committee's permission. The talent is still in these workshops, we just need to get out of our own way.

evening.text: You wouldn't run a workshop without a lock on the gate. Doesn't mean you hate the neighbours, just means you value what’s inside. Common sense, really.

morning.text: Morning. We used to engineer the world from workshops no bigger than my double garage. The grit is still here, we just need to put the clipboards down and remember what we can do.
